explanation: Only III is guaranteed by the inverse function theorem. At x=0, f is discontinuous, so the theorem does not apply. At x=-1, f(-1)=1 but f'(-1)=0, so the theorem does not guarantee a continuously differentiable inverse near y=1. At x=2, f(2)=0, f is continuously differentiable, and f'(2)≠0; hence the local inverse satisfies (f⁻¹)'(0)=1/f'(2).
